**Get information on individuals.**

Let's start from building the dataset with all the individuals we filmed (`ds_individuals`), where each row represents an individual. First, import the individuals for each time point, as each time point is saved in a different file.

```{r}
ds_individuals = NULL
for(time_point in time_points){
  
  # Import the master data (aka particles data) where particles in each video have been tracked.
  # We use time_point + 1 because our first time point is 0 and we cannot assign an object to ds_individuals[[0]], as the index of a dataset in R needs to be an integer >= 1. 
  
  ds_individuals[[time_point + 1]] = get(load(here("data",
                                                   "BEMOVI_output",
                                                   paste0(threshold, "_threshold_analysis"),
                                                   paste0("t", time_point),
                                                   merged_data_folder,
                                                   "Master.RData"))) %>%
    
    # To don't create rows with unnecessary NAs, remove the column "comment", as no entry received a comment in the experiment.
    
    mutate(comment = NULL,
           file = as.character(str_extract(file, "\\d+"))) %>%
    
    # To get rid of particles that are not protists, filter the dataset according to particles that are too slow (filter_min_net_disp), don't move for enough time (filter_min_duration), are not detected for an enough number of frames (filter_detection_freq), and ... (filter_median_step_length). 
    
    filter_data(.,
                filter_min_net_disp,
                filter_min_duration,
                filter_detection_freq,
                filter_median_step_length) %>%
    
    # To have each individual represented by a single row, link the same particle in different frames. 
    
    summarize_trajectories(.,
                           calculate.median = FALSE,
                           write = FALSE,
                           here("data", 
                                "BEMOVI_output",
                                paste0(threshold, "_threshold_analysis"), 
                                paste0("t", time_point), ""),
                                merged_data_folder) %>%
    
    # To don't have particles where some values couldn't be computed, remove rows that have NAs.
    
    filter(complete.cases(.)) %>%
    
    # To remember that some videos are replicates of the same ecosystem at a time point, introduce the column video_replicate. For all time points other than time point 0, it should be 1, as at each time point only a single video has been taken for each ecosystem. For time point 0, assign the value of file, which is the number of video that had been taken.
    
    mutate(video_replicate = ifelse(time_point > 0,
                                    as.character(1),
                                    as.character(file)),
           
    # To know which ecosystem was filmed, assign to ecosystem ID the value of file, as ecosystems were filmed in numerical order. Assign NA to videos at time point 0 because we filmed the master bottles of autotrophic and heterotrophic ecosystems and not the single ecosystems. 
           
           ecosystem_ID = ifelse(time_point > 0,
                                 as.character(file),
                                 as.character(NA))) %>%
    
    # To tidy up, reorder columns. 
    
    select(time_point, 
           day, 
           video_replicate, 
           file, 
           id, 
           everything())
}
```

Then, we need to do something a bit odd. When plotting ecosystems across time, we want to also to plot them at the day of the assembly (day 0). However, at day 0 instead of filming each ecosystem individually at this stage, we recorded the contents of the large bottles from which autotrophic and heterotrophic ecosystems were initiated. Hence, we do not have the data in the right format to be plotted at day 0. Therefore, we solve the problem by assigning to each autotrophic ecosystem the individuals filmed from the autotrophic bottle and to each heterotrophic ecosystem the individuals filmed from the heterotrophic bottle.

```{r}
ds_individuals_t0_extending = NULL

# Assign to every ecosystem the videos of its trophic type at time point 0.

for(ID in 1:n_ecosystems){
  
  ds_individuals_t0_extending[[ID]] = ds_individuals[[1]] %>%
    
    # To allocate the autotrophic videos to autotrophic ecosystems and the heterotrophic videos to heterotrophic ecosystems, choose autotrophic videos for autotrophic ecosystems and heterotrophic videos for heterotrophic ecosystems.
    
    filter((ID %in% ecosystem_IDs_autotrophic & trophic_type == "autotrophic") |
           (ID %in% ecosystem_IDs_heterotrophic & trophic_type == "heterotrophic")) %>%
    
    # To have more informative columns, manipulate them.
    
    mutate(file =  as.character(str_extract(file, "\\d+")),
           ecosystem_ID = as.character(ID),
    
    # To know that different individuals belong to different videos, add the column video replicates. The autotrophic videos start from video 1. The heterotrophic videos start from video 7. 
    
    video_replicate = as.character(file)) %>%
    
    # To tidy up, reorder columns.
    
    select(time_point, 
           day, 
           ecosystem_ID, 
           video_replicate, 
           file, 
           id, 
           everything())
}

# To have all the cultures at time point 0 in a single dataset, bind them together. 

ds_individuals[[1]] = ds_individuals_t0_extending %>%
  bind_rows()
```

Now that we have the individuals of all time points imported and in the right format (`ds_individuals[[1:5]]`), we can bind them all together in a single dataset (`ds_individuals`).

```{r}
ds_individuals = ds_individuals %>%
  bind_rows()
```

Let's then finish up the `ds_individuals` dataset by adjusting some columns and levels.

```{r}
ds_individuals = ds_individuals %>%
  mutate(
    
  # To avoid that trophic_type gives problems when combining ds_individuals with ecosystem_info, get rid of it, as it had the right value only at time point 0. 
  
    trophic_type = NULL,
    
  # To better work with ecosystem_ID, video_replicate, and file columns, transform them into a double format. 
  
         ecosystem_ID = as.double(str_extract(ecosystem_ID, "\\d+")),
         video_replicate = as.double(str_extract(video_replicate, "\\d+")),
         file = as.double(str_extract(file, "\\d+"))) %>%
  
  # To have all the information on the ecosystems that were not in the original data, bind 'ds_individuals' with 'ecosystem_info'.
  
  left_join(ecosystem_info,
            by = "ecosystem_ID") %>%
  
  # To make dataset clearer, rename columns.
  
  rename(ecosystem_type = eco_metaeco_type,
         ecosystem_size = patch_size,
         ecosystem_size_ml = patch_size_ml) %>%
  
  # To have everything in mm2 and ml, transform bioarea columns. 
  
  mutate(bioarea_µm2 = mean_area,
         bioarea_mm2 = bioarea_µm2 * 10^-6,
         bioarea_mm2_per_ml = bioarea_mm2 / volume_recorded_ml,
         bioarea_mm2_per_frame_per_ml = bioarea_mm2_per_ml * N_frames / total_frames,
         
  # To have levels that are easier to read, transform them. 
  
         ecosystem_type = case_when(ecosystem_type == "Sa" ~ "Small autotrophic disconnected",
                                    ecosystem_type == "Sh" ~ "Small heterotrophic disconnected",
                                    ecosystem_type == "Ma" ~ "Medium autotrophic disconnected",
                                    ecosystem_type == "Mh" ~ "Medium heterotrophic disconnected",
                                    ecosystem_type == "La" ~ "Large autotrophic disconnected",
                                    ecosystem_type == "Lh" ~ "Large heterotrophic disconnected",
                                    ecosystem_type == "Sa (Sa_Lh)" ~ "Small autotrophic connected",
                                    ecosystem_type == "Sh (Sh_La)" ~ "Small heterotrophic connected",
                                    ecosystem_type == "Ma (Ma_Mh)" ~ "Medium autotrophic connected",
                                    ecosystem_type == "Mh (Ma_Mh)" ~ "Medium heterotrophic connected",
                                    ecosystem_type == "La (Sh_La)" ~ "Large autotrophic connected",
                                    ecosystem_type == "Lh (Sa_Lh)" ~ "Large heterotrophic connected",
                                    TRUE ~ ecosystem_type),
         ecosystem_type = factor(ecosystem_type,
                                 levels = ecosystem_types_ordered),
         ecosystem_size = case_when(ecosystem_size == "S" ~ "Small",
                                    ecosystem_size == "M" ~ "Medium",
                                    ecosystem_size == "L" ~ "Large",
                                    TRUE ~ ecosystem_size),
         metaecosystem_type = case_when(metaecosystem_type == "Ma_Mh" ~ "ED connected",
                                        metaecosystem_type == "Sa_Lh" ~ "HD connected",
                                        metaecosystem_type == "Sh_La" ~ "AD connected",
                                        TRUE ~ metaecosystem_type),

  # To better plot and analyse data, add the columns connection and ecosystem_size_and_trophy.
  
         connection = factor(x = ifelse(metaecosystem == "yes",
                                        "connected",
                                        "disconnected"),
                             levels = connection_ordered),
         ecosystem_size_and_trophy = factor(x = paste(ecosystem_size, trophic_type),
                                            levels = ecosystem_size_and_trophy_ordered)) %>%
  
  # To tidy up, reorder columns. 
  
  select(time_point,
         day,
         video_replicate,
         ecosystem_ID,
         system_nr,
         ecosystem_type,
         ecosystem_size,
         ecosystem_size_ml,
         trophic_type,
         ecosystem_size_and_trophy,
         metaecosystem,
         metaecosystem_type,
         connection,
         bioarea_mm2,
         bioarea_mm2_per_frame_per_ml,
         N_frames,
         all_of(columns_for_species_ID))
```
